en.title: The Sierra storm reaches Utah: 1 to 2 feet for the Wasatch from Alta and Snowbird to Snowbasin
en.description: The National Weather Service expects 10 to 20 inches in the Wasatch from Thursday to Saturday. Where Utah's snowpack stands against past winters, why Utah snow is lighter, and when to ski.
en.lede: After burying the Sierra, the storm is crossing Nevada and reaching Utah in pieces from Thursday to Saturday, 19 to 21 November 2026. The National Weather Service has a Winter Weather Advisory for the Wasatch Mountains with 10 to 20 inches of snow, locally more in the upper Cottonwoods, and its forecasters say a general 1 to 2 feet looks right for the northern mountains. Unlike the Sierra, Utah starts from a roughly normal snowpack, so this storm turns an ordinary start into a good one.

p: The Salt Lake City office explains it like this: the low-pressure system that brought the atmospheric river to California is opening into a trough and crossing Utah in pieces. The first wave on Thursday comes in on southwest winds, with mild air and a snow level between 5,000 and 6,500 ft, which favours the northern Wasatch and the southern mountains. After a lull on Friday, a second wave on Friday evening turns the wind to the northwest, brings colder air and lowers the snow level to the valley floors, and that flow favours the central Wasatch, Little and Big Cottonwood Canyons.

By the time the moisture reaches Utah it has already dropped much of its water on the Sierra and the Nevada ranges, so totals are smaller. But Utah's snow is usually drier and lighter. The gauges show it: at Brighton, 10 inches of new snow held 1.1 inches of water, about 9 to 1, and at Mill-D North it was 12 to 1, compared with 4 to 9 to 1 at the Sierra gauges this week.

Our snow maps give about 12 inches (30 cm) from Thursday to Saturday at the upper slopes of Alta and Snowbird, 11 inches (29 cm) at Brighton and Solitude, 13 inches (33 cm) at Snowbasin, 11 inches (28 cm) at Powder Mountain, and 8 inches at Park City and Deer Valley on the drier Wasatch Back. Friday, 20 November, is the snowiest day on our maps, with about 7 inches at Alta and 8 inches at Snowbasin.

The weather service is more generous: 10 to 20 inches for the Wasatch, 4 to 8 inches for the Park City area and the Ogden Valley, and even its lower-end forecast exceeds 20 inches locally on the Wasatch and the Bear River Range. Our numbers sit at the low end of that, so treat a foot as the likely amount and more as possible.

sections.h: Where Utah's snowpack stands against past winters
p: Before this storm the gauges had already caught snow on Tuesday and Wednesday: between Tuesday and Thursday morning, Atwater above Alta went from 5 to 17 inches, the Snowbird gauge from 8 to 18 inches and Brighton from 1 to 11 inches. Even so, the water in the snowpack is only about normal: 100 % of the usual for the date at Snowbird, 62 % at Brighton, 76 % at Thaynes Canyon above Park City and 125 % at Little Bear in the Ogden Valley.

Our past-winters comparison says the same. At mid-mountain Alta has about 29 inches (73 cm), against a usual 18 inches on 19 November, and 12 of the past 46 winters were deeper. Brighton, Solitude and Park City are right at normal, about the middle of the 46 winters. The big early starts in Utah were 1984-85, with about 70 inches at Alta on this date, and 1996-97, with 59 inches. This is a decent start, not a historic one, which is exactly why this storm matters.

sections.h: When to ski, and what to watch
p: Saturday morning, 21 November, after the colder second wave, should give the best snow in the Cottonwoods; Sunday 22 November looks dry on our maps. Expect winter driving on Friday morning and Saturday, especially in Little and Big Cottonwood Canyons, where traction rules and road closures for avalanche control are common in storms. Check the canyon road status before you go.

Thin early-season snow plus a storm on top is the setup avalanche forecasters watch most closely. Inside the resorts, terrain opens as patrol finishes its work; outside, read the Utah Avalanche Center forecast before going anywhere steep.

sections.h: Plan the trip for the clear days
p: Our trip planner compares Snowbird, Park City and the other big western resorts on snow, lift ticket, places to stay and food for your dates and budget. We set it to Saturday 21 to Tuesday 24 November, three nights, the first days after the storm.
